question: Which type of soil is found on about 40% of the total area of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Alluvial soil**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alluvial soil** is found on about 40% of the total area of India.
 
• This type of soil is primarily found in the plains of the northern and coastal regions of India.
 
• Alluvial soil is highly fertile and suitable for growing a variety of crops, including rice, wheat, sugarcane, and cotton.
 
• The soil is deposited by rivers and is rich in nutrients like potash, phosphoric acid, and lime.
 
• It supports extensive agricultural activities and is a significant contributor to India's agrarian economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Alluvial soil is divided into two types: **New alluvium (Khadar)** and **Old alluvium (Bhangar)**.
 
• **Khadar soil** is found in the floodplains of rivers and is renewed annually by fresh silt deposits.
 
• **Bhangar soil** is found on higher terraces and is older, with higher concentrations of clay and organic matter.
 
• These soils are especially predominant in the Indo-Gangetic Plain, which includes states like Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and West Bengal.
 
• The fertility of alluvial soil makes it a crucial resource for India's food security and agricultural productivity.
